passages.title: Office Memo — Hybrid Work Policy
passages.text:
TO: All Staff
FROM: Human Resources
SUBJECT: Updated Hybrid Work Policy

Effective the first of November, all full-time employees will be eligible for two remote work days per week. The new schedule (1)____ approval from each employee's direct manager before implementation. Department heads must also (2)____ that critical in-office coverage is maintained on weekdays.

blanks.exp: 主語 The new schedule は単数で現在の規定なので requires が正解。
must の後は動詞原形なので ensure が正解。
分詞構文と並行する継続「〜しながら」を表す while が自然。

ch: Questions about your individual eligibility should be directed to Human Resources.
All managers will receive a separate budget allocation for hybrid-work equipment.
The previous policy will remain unchanged until further notice.
New employees are not subject to the standard probation review.

singles.text:
GreenLine Logistics Wins National Sustainability Award

GreenLine Logistics has been awarded the 2026 National Green Operations Prize for its industry-leading reduction in carbon emissions across long-haul shipping. According to the awarding committee, the company achieved a 42 percent reduction over five years, the largest drop reported by any major logistics provider this year.

CEO Marina Ito accepted the award at a ceremony in Tokyo on Tuesday and thanked the engineering team for retrofitting nearly two hundred trucks with hybrid powertrains. Ito noted that the next phase will focus on transitioning the regional delivery fleet to fully electric vehicles by 2029.

The award includes a research grant of fifty million yen, which the company plans to invest in alternative fuel development.

ch: The lowest delivery cost in its industry
A 42 percent reduction in emissions over five years
A doubling of its truck fleet

Building a new headquarters in Tokyo
Listing on a new stock exchange

questions.exp: 末文に「invest in alternative fuel development」と明記。

singles.title: Online customer review
singles.text:
★★★★☆ — Reviewed by Daniela R., verified buyer

I bought the EcoMug travel cup for my daily commute and have been using it for six weeks. The insulation works exactly as advertised — my coffee stayed warm for nearly five hours during a long morning meeting. The cup is also surprisingly light and easy to clean.

My only minor complaint is that the lid sometimes leaks when carried sideways in a backpack. I had to upgrade to the optional silicone sleeve to fully prevent spills. The sleeve is sold separately for about 800 yen.

Overall, I would still recommend EcoMug for office workers who want a reliable, sustainable alternative to disposable cups.

New Ferry Service Connects Hakata and Busan

A new high-speed ferry service between Hakata Port and Busan launched yesterday, reducing travel time between the two cities to just three hours. The operator, Tsushima Express Line, will run two round trips daily.

One-way tickets begin at 12,800 yen for standard cabins, with premium cabins available from 22,000 yen. According to the company, the new vessel can carry up to four hundred passengers and includes a small restaurant offering Korean and Japanese cuisine.

Industry analysts say the service is expected to boost tourism in both regions, particularly during peak holiday seasons. The company plans to add a third daily round trip if demand exceeds projections during the first quarter of operation.

singles.text:
Quarterly Travel Sentiment Report — Highlights

In this quarter's regional travel sentiment survey, 67 percent of respondents said they planned to take at least one international trip in the next six months — the highest level recorded in two years. Sustainability also remained an important factor: 54 percent reported they would pay slightly more for eco-certified accommodation.

Top destinations cited included Singapore, Vietnam, and Italy. Notably, interest in winter travel to Scandinavia rose by 18 percentage points compared with the previous quarter.

The full report and methodology are available on our website. The next survey will close to participants on January 15.

passages.label: Newsletter article

Coral Star Renews Pacific Voyages with All-Electric Hybrid Fleet

Coral Star Cruises announced today that all four of its Pacific-route vessels will be refitted with hybrid electric propulsion by the end of 2027. The retrofit, valued at 12 billion yen, is the company's largest sustainability investment to date and is expected to reduce per-voyage carbon emissions by an average of 38 percent.

During the refit period, three ships will remain in service while the fourth, MV Aurora Star, enters dry dock from June 1 to August 31. Routes normally served by MV Aurora Star will be temporarily covered by chartered partner vessels, with no changes to scheduled departure dates.

During the dry-dock period (June 1 - August 31), affected passengers will sail aboard our partner vessel, MV Pacific Crown. Cabin categories will match as closely as possible to your original booking, and all included excursions remain unchanged.

As a goodwill gesture, every passenger will receive a 20,000 yen onboard credit, redeemable for dining, spa, or boutique purchases. No additional action is required on your part; replacement boarding passes will be emailed two weeks before departure.
